---
title: "Weekly commodity prices: snapshots, charts, and archives"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Weekly commodity prices: snapshots, charts, and archives}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

`read_agau_prices()` is for workflows that need a dated Weekly commodity
price snapshot while retaining the table or chart series, published unit,
provider, and source hash. It can parse the current HTML table and accessible
charts, an exact historical HTML/PDF/Word/text snapshot, or a quarterly ZIP
containing supported assets.

The examples below are fully offline. The files under
`inst/fixtures/html`, `inst/fixtures/text`, and `inst/fixtures/pdf` are
package-owned synthetic fixtures designed to exercise parser profiles. They
are not official price observations, even when their column names or source
provider labels resemble the upstream publication. Live source URLs in the
catalogue are metadata for discovery and attribution, not bundled source
values.

## Parse the current table and chart profile

The current profile is split across one table page and three pages containing
accessible chart descriptions. Supplying the local paths together lets the
same reader exercise both branches without network access.

```{r setup}
library(readagau)

fixture_root <- system.file("fixtures", package = "readagau")
weekly_html <- file.path(
  fixture_root,
  "html",
  c(
    "weekly-prices-current.html",
    "weekly-world-charts.html",
    "weekly-australian-charts.html",
    "weekly-horticulture-charts.html"
  )
)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(weekly_html)))

weekly_cache <- tempfile("readagau-weekly-prices-")
dir.create(weekly_cache)

current <- read_agau_prices(
  snapshot = weekly_html,
  series = c("A2", "H1"),
  measures = c("latest_price", "annual_change"),
  cache_dir = weekly_cache
)
```

`series` accepts canonical IDs such as `A2` (a world series) and `H1` (a
horticulture series). The current table contributes its published measures;
the chart pages contribute dated `latest_price` observations. A small view
keeps the distinction visible:

```{r current-preview}
current[
  , c(
    "release_date", "table_id", "record_role", "period",
    "observation_date", "value", "unit", "source_asset"
  )
]
```

The returned object has class `agau_weekly_prices` (and `agau_data`). Its
common observation contract includes `product`, `release_id`, `release_date`,
`table_id`, `record_role`, `period`, `period_start`, `period_end`,
`period_status`, `unit`, `value`, `raw_value`, `missing_reason`,
`observation_key`, `source_provider`, `rights_status`, `sha256`, and
`parser_version`. `observation_date` records the date stated by an
accessible chart when it differs from the release date; `snapshot_date`
records the dated snapshot context.

The full semantic registry can be inspected without parsing a source:

```{r series-catalogue}
weekly_series <- agau_series_catalog("weekly_commodity_prices")
weekly_series[
  weekly_series$source_series_id %in% c("A2", "H1"),
  c("source_series_id", "indicator", "commodity", "market", "source_provider")
]
```

## Read an exact historical snapshot

Exact local paths are preferable for reproducible analyses. A text extract is
one supported historical profile; the result retains the report date and the
asset name rather than inferring identity from a renamed file.

```{r exact-text}
historical_file <- file.path(
  fixture_root, "text", "weekly-2025-07-10.txt"
)
historical <- read_agau_prices(
  snapshot = historical_file,
  series = "A2",
  measures = c("latest_price", "annual_change"),
  cache_dir = weekly_cache
)
historical[
  , c(
    "release_id", "release_date", "table_id", "record_role",
    "period", "value", "unit", "source_provider", "sha256"
  )
]
```

The same API accepts a vector of exact paths, including an HTML page, a text
extract, a Word document, or a supported ZIP. `snapshot = "all"` is a
catalogue-driven operation and therefore requires the official archive
assets; it is intentionally not used in the deterministic example above.

## Optional PDF parsing

PDF parsing uses the external `pdftotext` executable supplied by Poppler. The
dependency is optional for non-PDF workflows: a missing executable should be
reported to the user and does not prevent the HTML or text readers from being
used. This chunk runs only when both a packaged PDF fixture and Poppler are
available, so a CRAN check on a platform without Poppler remains deterministic.

```{r optional-pdf}
pdf_file <- file.path(fixture_root, "pdf", "weekly-2016-10-13.pdf")
pdf_ready <- file.exists(pdf_file) && nzchar(Sys.which("pdftotext"))

pdf_preview <- if (pdf_ready) {
  pdf_data <- read_agau_prices(
    snapshot = pdf_file,
    series = "A2",
    measures = c("latest_price", "annual_change"),
    cache_dir = weekly_cache
  )
  pdf_data[
    , c("release_date", "table_id", "record_role", "value", "unit")
  ]
} else {
  data.frame(
    status = "PDF example skipped: packaged PDF or pdftotext is unavailable",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
pdf_preview
```

## Typed failures, cache, and live calls

Unknown or unsupported snapshot IDs produce an `agau_asset_missing_error`
rather than a partially parsed result. This is useful in scheduled jobs,
where a missing archive should be retried or escalated explicitly.

```{r typed-failure}
missing_snapshot <- tryCatch(
  read_agau_prices(
    snapshot = "synthetic-release-not-in-catalogue",
    cache_dir = weekly_cache
  ),
  agau_asset_missing_error = function(e) e
)
stopifnot(inherits(missing_snapshot, "agau_asset_missing_error"))
missing_snapshot
```

For live calls, `snapshot = "latest"` discovers the current landing page and
then caches immutable raw assets under `cache_dir`; `refresh = TRUE` is an
explicit request to refresh discovery and bytes. Choose a cache below
`tempdir()` for examples and tests, or `agau_cache_dir()` for a user-managed
application cache. Live calls can change as the publisher updates its page,
and upstream providers may have their own terms and availability.

The live path is deliberately opt-in. It is not evaluated during ordinary
non-interactive vignette or CRAN builds, and it should only be enabled after
checking network access and current source terms:

```{r live-weekly, eval=TRUE}
if (interactive() && identical(Sys.getenv("READAGAU_RUN_LIVE"), "true")) {
  live_weekly <- read_agau_prices(
    snapshot = "latest",
    include_charts = FALSE,
    cache_dir = weekly_cache
  )
  utils::head(live_weekly)
}
```

The offline fixtures above are the reproducible path for examples, tests, and
package checks; they intentionally do not make claims about the current
official prices.
